To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the asymmetric emittance beam can be obtained by using round beam RF photo injectors and non linear optics.
it is possible to generate asymmetric beams with a round beam RF gun and a sextupolar triplet.
it is possible to generate flat beams from a round beam using a round beam RF gun and non-linear optics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the beam dynamics of a round beam, generated by an RF gun, in a transport system consisting of a quadrupole double and a sextupolar triplet.
the design of a new generation of high brightness RF photo-injector, able to generate beams with asymmetric emittances.

- the design of a new generation of high brightness RF photo-injector, based on the use of a new RF structure, the disk-loaded waveguide; - the development of an innovative technique, based on the non-linear optics of the beam, to generate asymmetric beams; - the study of the beam transport line to the storage rings, in particular the design of a compact and efficient beam transport line to match the TTF storage ring.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TESLA collider requirements are not achievable with the present status of the RF gun technology.
the use of sextupole tripletes, in conjunction with round-beam photo-injectors (e.g. RF guns), can provide asymmetric beams with the required emittance.

, in order to produce flat asymmetric beams, a round beam RF gun, in conjunction with a sextupole triple, is the best solution, even if the beam emittance at the gun exit is larger than the TESLA specification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the TESLA requirements can be met with a 1.6 cell 1.3 GHz S-band photo-injector, provided that the beam energy is increased to 20 MeV, and a quadrupole sextupole doublet triplet is placed in the beam transport line.
the TESLA requirements can be fulfilled by a 1.6 cell RF gun, a 3.5 cell RF gun and a 5 cell RF gun with sextupole triplet emittance correctors, respectively.
the TESLA asymmetric emittance requirements can be met with a round beam RF gun, if the beam energy is high enough, and if a proper beam transport is designed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of sextupoles is a promising approach to produce asymmetric beams from round-beam RF photo-injector.
it is possible to produce asymmetric beams, even if the gun emittance is dominated by linear effects.
the TESLA requirements on the normalized rms transverse beam emittances are attainable using a conventional RF gun and non-linear optics.
